definition_zh: 古代的；古老的；年代久远的；古人；过时的
definition_en: belonging to a time long past, especially to the civilizations before the Middle Ages; also very old
core_image: 石墙上爬满青苔，碑文被风磨得只剩浅浅的凹痕
scene: 博物馆的展柜里，一只陶罐裂成几片，旁边的标签写着出土地点。Visitors gathered around the ancient vase, wondering who had made it.
sceneCN: 这里 ancient 是「古代的、年代久远的」（第 1 个义项：属于久远年代的器物）；句意为参观者围在这只古老陶罐旁，猜想它出自谁手。画面里有展柜、裂开的陶罐与标签。

pos.zh: 形容词：古代的；古老的；年代久远的；过时的
名词（常用复数 the ancients）：古人；古代民族

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 antiquitas 借入，义为「古代；古物」，与本词同出表示「从前」的词根
由拉丁语 antiquus 经法语借入，义为「古董的；古董」，与本词是同一词根的另一支
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在古代；古时」

senses.title: Belonging to the distant past
senses.definition: belonging to a civilization or period long before the present, especially before the Middle Ages
senses.definitionCN: 属于很久以前、尤指中世纪以前的文明或时期
senses.example: Visitors gathered around the ancient vase, wondering who had made it.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者围在这只古老陶罐旁，猜想它出自谁手。
senses.why: Ante means before: whatever belongs to the time before everything familiar is ancient.
senses.whyCN: ante 意为「以前」：凡是属于一切熟悉事物之前那段时间的东西，就是「古代的」。

senses.title: Extremely old in years
senses.definition: having existed for a very long time, used of trees, buildings or objects
senses.definitionCN: 已经存在很久，用于树木、建筑或器物
senses.example: The ancient oak still stands at the centre of the square.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵古老的橡树仍立在广场中央。
senses.why: The same 'before' idea applied to a single thing: its beginning lies far back in time.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「以前」的观念用在一件东西上：它的起点远在时间深处。

senses.title: The people of early civilizations
senses.definition: in the plural, the peoples and writers of early civilizations
senses.definitionCN: 用复数形式，指早期文明中的民族与著作家
senses.example: The ancients believed the stars moved around the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 古人相信群星绕地球运行。
senses.why: A whole era is compressed into its people: those who lived before are simply the ancients.
senses.whyCN: 整个时代被压缩成那个时代的人：生活在以前的人，直接就被称为「古人」。

senses.title: Long established
senses.titleCN: 历史悠久的；沿袭已久的
senses.definition: established so long ago that it seems part of the place or group
senses.definitionCN: 确立得极早，仿佛已经成为地方或群体的一部分
senses.example: The village keeps an ancient custom of sharing the first harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子保留着分享首季收成的古老习俗。
senses.why: A custom whose beginning is forgotten feels as old as the ground it stands on.
senses.whyCN: 一项习俗若连起点都被遗忘，就会显得和它扎根的土地一样古老。

senses.title: Hopelessly out of date
senses.definition: used humorously or critically for ideas or methods that belong to an earlier age
senses.definitionCN: 带幽默或批评意味，指属于过去时代的思想或方法
senses.example: His arguments about office work sound ancient to new graduates.
senses.exampleCN: 在新毕业生听来，他关于办公室工作的论点老掉牙了。
senses.why: The boundary of 'before' can be brought forward: anything that belongs to yesterday's world is jokingly ancient.
senses.whyCN: 「以前」的界线可以被往前挪：凡是属于昨日世界的东西，都能被戏称为「古代」。

intro.en: Ancient goes back to a Latin word for before, and its cousin antique took a separate road through French.
intro.cn: ancient 追溯到拉丁语中表示「以前」的词，它的表亲 antique 走了另一条法语路径。

items.en: The preposition and adverb ante meant 'before, in front of'. It is the time word at the back of the family.
items.cn: 介词与副词 ante 意为「在……之前、在前面」，是这一词族背后的时间词。

items.en: A form generally reconstructed as *anteanus 'from before' developed in everyday Latin. This form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语中发展出一般重构为 *anteanus「来自以前的」的形式。该形式属重构，不是有记录的词。

items.en: Old French ancien continued that form and meant 'former, old, of long ago'.
items.cn: 古法语 ancien 延续这一形式，意为「从前的、旧的、很久以前的」。

items.en: English borrowed ancien as ancient; the exact first date is uncertain because spelling varied widely.
items.cn: 英语把 ancien 借入为 ancient；由于早期拼写差异很大，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The separate Latin adjective antiquus 'old, former' produced antique through French, so ancient and antique are cousins rather than the same word.
items.cn: 另一个拉丁形容词 antiquus「旧的、从前的」经法语产生 antique，因此 ancient 与 antique 是表亲，而不是同一个词。

items.en: Ancient now covers early civilizations, very old objects, the peoples of the past, long traditions and, humorously, out-of-date ideas.
items.cn: 今天 ancient 覆盖早期文明、极古老的器物、过去的民族、悠久的传统，以及带幽默意味的过时观念。

note.en: The look-alike group is the before-family and its antique cousin; the near-meaning group gathers words for age and historical distance.
note.cn: 形近组收表示「以前」的词族及其 antique 表亲；近义组收表示年岁与历史距离的词。

entries.definition: The distant past, especially the civilizations of Greece and Rome, or an object from that time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「古代、古物」，尤指希腊罗马文明或那个时代的器物，与本词同根。

entries.definition: An object from an earlier period, or an adjective meaning old-fashioned; from Latin antiquus, a cousin rather than the direct source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「古董；古董的」，来自拉丁语 antiquus，与本词是同一词根的另一支，并非直接来源。

entries.definition: Adverb: in ancient times, long ago.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在古代、古时」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Having lived or existed for a long time; the plain everyday word, with no historical scale.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老的、旧的」，是最日常的说法，不带历史尺度。

entries.definition: Important in history, or preserved from it; about significance rather than great age.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有历史意义的、历史性的」，强调重要性而非年代久远。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier stage of a language or practice and no longer current.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「古体的、过时的」，指属于语言或做法的早期阶段，现已不用。

entries.definition: Belonging to the time before written records, older than ancient in the technical scale.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「史前的」，指有文字记录之前，比古代的年代更早。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin word for before and the separate road taken by antique.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语中表示「以前」的词，以及 antique 走过的另一条路。

normal.en: Ante is before: ancient time is the time before everything we know.
normal.cn: ante 是「以前」：古代就是我们熟悉的一切之前的那段时间。

normal.en: Old French ancien carried the word into English with the meaning former and old.
normal.cn: 古法语 ancien 把这个词带进英语，意思是「从前的、旧的」。

normal.en: Antique came by a different road from Latin antiquus; the two words are cousins, not twins.
normal.cn: antique 从拉丁语 antiquus 走另一条路而来；两词是表亲，不是双胞胎。

normal.en: The ancients means the peoples of early civilizations, treated as one collective person.
normal.cn: the ancients 指早期文明的民族，被当作一个集体的人来看待。

normal.en: Archaic is stricter than ancient: it marks something a language has already dropped.
normal.cn: archaic 比 ancient 更严格：它标出语言已经弃用的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a stone wall under moss, its carved letters almost worn away by rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一面长满青苔的石墙，刻字被雨水磨得几乎看不见。

abstract.en: Picture a line of footprints fading into dust, each one older than the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一串脚印渐渐隐入尘土，一个比一个更早。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands stopped centuries ago but whose frame still stands in the square.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟，指针在几百年前就停了，钟架却仍立在广场上。

examples.cn: 参观者围在这只古老陶罐旁，猜想它出自谁手。

examples.en: The ancient oak still stands at the centre of the square.

examples.en: The village keeps an ancient custom of sharing the first harvest.
examples.cn: 这个村子保留着分享首季收成的古老习俗。

root: 拉丁语 ante「在……之前」是这一词族的时间词；通俗拉丁语中一般重构出 *anteanus「来自以前的」，经古法语 ancien 进入英语成为 ancient。另一个拉丁形容词 antiquus「旧的」经法语产生 antique，两词是同根表亲，并非同一个词。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all measure distance from the present: a civilization, an old object, the people of that era, a long tradition, and jokingly anything that feels out of date.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都在衡量与此刻的距离：一个文明、一件旧物、那个时代的人、一项悠久的传统，以及被戏称为过时的任何东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved stone stands in the square, its letters worn shallow by centuries of weather.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刻字的石头立在广场上，字迹被数百年的风雨磨浅。

branches.en: THE CIVILIZATION LINE: the era before the familiar world, with its own states and monuments.
branches.cn: 文明线：熟悉世界之前的那段时代，有自己的国家与纪念建筑。

branches.en: THE OBJECT LINE: one thing whose beginning lies very far back.
branches.cn: 器物线：一件东西的起点远在时间深处。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE LINE: the era compressed into the people who lived in it.
branches.cn: 人物线：整个时代被压缩成生活在其中的人。

branches.en: THE TRADITION LINE: a practice whose origin has been forgotten.
branches.cn: 传统线：一项连起源都被遗忘的做法。

branches.en: THE HUMOUR LINE: the boundary of before is moved forward until yesterday counts as ancient.
branches.cn: 幽默线：把「以前」的界线挪到昨天，让昨日之物也被戏称为古代。

intro.en: Ancient is a Latin before-word carried through French; its endings are ordinary English adjective and noun endings.
intro.cn: ancient 是一个拉丁语「以前」的词经法语带入英语，词尾是普通的英语形容词与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ante, antiquus and antiquitas are recorded; only the Vulgar Latin intermediate is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ante、antiquus 与 antiquitas 都有记录，只有中间的通俗拉丁语形式属于重构。

items.example: It now covers civilizations, objects and peoples.

items.example: It is the cousin root behind antique.

items.meaning: the ancient past; an old object
items.example: It names the era itself rather than a thing in it.
items.exampleCN: 它命名的是时代本身，而不是时代里的某件东西。

items.meaning: in the stated manner or time

items.example: It forms the noun ancients.

definition_zh: 和；与；然后；于是；而；用于数字连接与固定结构
definition_en: a conjunction that joins words, phrases or clauses, marking addition, sequence, result or contrast
core_image: 两只手各拿一样东西，被同一根绳子系在一起
scene: 厨房里，母亲把面粉和鸡蛋摆上案板，孩子踮着脚在旁边看。She mixed the flour and the eggs in a large blue bowl.
sceneCN: 这里 and 是「和、与」（第 1 个义项：连接两个并列成分）；句意为她把面粉和鸡蛋放进一只蓝色大碗里搅拌。画面里有厨房案板、面粉、鸡蛋与踮脚观看的孩子。

pos.zh: 连词：和；与；然后；于是；而

derivatives.zh: 由 and 与 or 用斜线连接而成的复合连词，义为「和／或」，用于正式文本
由本词加 then 构成的固定短语，义为「然后、接着」
由本词加 so 与 on 构成的固定短语，义为「等等」

senses.title: Joining words of the same kind
senses.definition: used to join two or more words, phrases or clauses that have the same grammatical role
senses.definitionCN: 用于连接两个或更多语法作用相同的词、短语或从句
senses.example: She mixed the flour and the eggs in a large blue bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她把面粉和鸡蛋放进一只蓝色大碗里搅拌。
senses.why: Old English and simply meant 'thereupon, together with'; the basic job is to tie two equal things into one pair.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 and 本义就是「连同、和」，最基本的任务是把两个同等的东西绑成一对。

senses.title: Marking a sequence of actions
senses.definition: used between two actions to show that the second follows the first
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个动作之间，表示第二个动作接在第一个之后
senses.example: He opened the window and let the cold air in.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开窗户，让冷空气进来。
senses.why: Two events placed side by side are read in time order, so simple addition becomes sequence.
senses.whyCN: 两件事并排放着，人自然会按时间顺序去读，于是单纯的「相加」变成了「先后」。

senses.title: Marking a result
senses.definition: used to introduce a consequence of what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出刚刚所说内容带来的后果
senses.example: She spoke quietly and everyone in the room fell silent.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻声说话，于是屋里所有人都安静下来。
senses.why: When the second event is caused by the first, the same joining word carries a causal colour.
senses.whyCN: 当第二件事由第一件事造成时，同一个连接词就带上了因果色彩。

senses.title: Marking contrast
senses.definition: used to balance two contrasting facts or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 用于平衡两个相互对照的事实或性质
senses.example: The room was small and the garden was enormous.
senses.exampleCN: 房间很小，而花园却极大。
senses.why: Two items can be joined while pulling in opposite directions; the tie itself then marks the contrast.
senses.whyCN: 两件事可以被系在一起，却朝相反方向拉；这时这根绳子本身就标示了对比。

senses.title: In numbers
senses.definition: used between hundreds and tens or units in spoken and written numbers
senses.definitionCN: 在口头或书面数字中，用于连接百位与十位或个位
senses.example: The old bridge is one hundred and five years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老桥已经有一百零五年了。
senses.why: The number is built like a phrase, and the conjunction marks the step down from hundreds to the rest.
senses.whyCN: 数字像短语一样被搭起来，连词标出从百位降到其余位的那一步。

senses.title: In fixed intensifying patterns
senses.titleCN: 用于固定结构加强语气
senses.definition: used in patterns such as nice and warm or good and ready, where it strengthens the second adjective
senses.definitionCN: 用于 nice and warm、good and ready 等结构，加强后一个形容词的语气
senses.example: The kitchen was nice and warm after the fire was lit.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火点起后，厨房又暖和又舒服。
senses.why: The two adjectives are joined so tightly that the first becomes an intensifier of the second.
senses.whyCN: 两个形容词被系得太紧，以至于第一个变成了第二个的加强成分。

intro.en: And is one of the oldest words in English, and its deeper origin is genuinely uncertain.
intro.cn: and 是英语里最古老的词之一，它更早的来源确实不清楚。

items.en: The conjunction appears as and and ond, joining words and clauses much as it does today.
items.cn: 这个连词在古英语中写作 and 与 ond，连接词与从句的方式与今天相近。

items.en: The reconstructed form *andi is the common Germanic source; it is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 重构形式 *andi 是共同的日耳曼语来源；它属重构，不是有记录的词。

items.en: The deeper Indo-European connections of and are disputed. Some older suggestions link it to a root meaning 'facing, against', but this is not established.
items.cn: and 更早的印欧语联系存在争议。较早的说法曾把它与表示「面对、相对」的词根相联系，但这并未确立。

items.en: The spelling settles as and, while the variant ond disappears from ordinary prose.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 and，变体 ond 从普通散文中消失。

items.en: The word expands into fixed patterns such as and so on and nice and warm, and into compounds such as and/or.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到 and so on、nice and warm 等固定结构，也进入 and/or 这类复合形式。

note.en: The look-alike group is spelling only, with no shared origin; the near-meaning group gathers connectors and companions of addition.
note.cn: 形近组只在拼写上相近，没有共同来源；近义组收表示添加、伴随与转折的连接词。

entries.definition: A group of musicians or a strip of material; it contains and by spelling only and has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「乐队、带子」，只是拼写里含有 and，词源完全不同。

entries.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm; no historical connection with the conjunction.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手」，与这个连词没有历史联系，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: Tiny grains of rock; it merely ends in the same letters.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沙子」，只是结尾字母相同，词源无关。

entries.definition: The solid surface of the earth; another spelling neighbour with no shared origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「土地；着陆」，是另一个仅拼写相近的词，词源无关。

entries.definition: Added to; used in maths and in informal lists, more explicit than and.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或连词，义为「加上」，用于数学与口语列举，比 and 更明确表示添加。

entries.definition: In addition; an adverb that adds a whole statement rather than joining two words.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「也、还」，添加的是一整句话，而不是连接两个词。

entries.definition: Accompanied by; a preposition of company rather than a conjunction of equality.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「和……一起」，表示伴随，而不是连接两个对等成分。

entries.definition: A conjunction of contrast; it occupies the same slot as and but pulls the other way.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「但是」，占据与 and 相同的位置，方向却相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English forms and the fixed patterns the word now lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的古英语形式，以及这个词今天所处的固定结构。

normal.en: Old English had and and ond; the shorter spelling won.
normal.cn: 古英语有 and 与 ond 两种形式，最终较短的那个胜出。

normal.en: The deeper origin is uncertain, so do not invent a root for it.
normal.cn: 更早的来源不确定，不要替它编造词根。

normal.en: Two words joined by and become one pair, like two handles tied by a rope.
normal.cn: 两个词被 and 一连就成一对，像两个把手被一根绳子系住。

normal.en: In numbers, and marks the step from hundreds down to tens and units.
normal.cn: 在数字里，and 标出从百位降到十位与个位的那一步。

normal.en: Nice and warm is a fixed pattern: the first adjective strengthens the second.
normal.cn: nice and warm 是固定结构：第一个形容词加强第二个。

abstract.en: Picture two hands each holding a small object, a single rope running between the wrists.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手各拿一件小东西，一根绳子在两只手腕之间连着。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge of one plank laid between two banks, letting either side reach the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板搭在两岸之间，让任何一边都能到达另一边。

abstract.en: Picture two beads sliding onto one string until they click together in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象两颗珠子滑向同一根线，最后在中间轻轻碰在一起。

examples.en: She mixed the flour and the eggs in a large blue bowl.
examples.cn: 她把面粉和鸡蛋放进一只蓝色大碗里搅拌。

examples.en: He opened the window and let the cold air in.
examples.cn: 他打开窗户，让冷空气进来。

examples.en: The old bridge is one hundred and five years old.
examples.cn: 这座老桥已经有一百零五年了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的」——把两样东西安安稳稳地系在一起：和、与

root: 古英语连词 and、ond 是这个词的直接来源，可追溯到重构的原始日耳曼语形式 *andi；更早的印欧语联系存在争议，一种旧说把它与表示「面对、相对」的词根相联系，但未确立。现代英语中它扩展出 and so on、nice and warm、and/or 等固定结构。

sensesIntro.en: Six uses of one rope: joining equals, marking sequence, marking result, marking contrast, building numbers, and intensifying a fixed pair of adjectives.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根绳子的六种用法：连接对等成分、表示先后、表示结果、表示对比、搭建数字，以及加强一对固定搭配的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two objects are tied by one rope and become a pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西被同一根绳子系住，成为一对。

branches.en: THE PAIR LINE: two equal words or phrases are joined into one unit.
branches.cn: 对等线：两个平等的词或短语被连成一个单位。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: two actions joined are read one after the other.
branches.cn: 时间线：两个动作一相连，就被读成先后发生。

branches.en: THE CAUSE LINE: the second event is heard as the consequence of the first.
branches.cn: 因果线：第二件事被听成第一件事的后果。

branches.en: THE OPPOSITE LINE: the rope joins two facts that pull in different directions.
branches.cn: 对照线：绳子连起两个朝相反方向拉的事实。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND PATTERN LINE: the same tie builds a spoken number or an intensified adjective pair.
branches.cn: 数字与结构线：同一根系绳既搭出口语数字，也加强一对形容词。

intro.en: And has no derivational affixes; its construction history is a stable conjunction plus fixed phrases and compounds.
intro.cn: and 没有派生词缀；它的构词史是一个稳定的连词，加上若干固定短语与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate established for and, so the Latin side is left empty rather than filled with a guess.
latinIntro.cn: and 没有已确立的拉丁同源词，因此拉丁部分留空，不用猜测填补。

definition_zh: 愤怒；怒气；义愤；使发怒；激怒
definition_en: a strong feeling of displeasure caused by something unfair, hurtful or frustrating; also to make someone feel this
core_image: 胸口一团越收越紧的热，最后从喉咙冲出来
scene: 修车铺里，车主发现刚换的零件又坏了，拳头慢慢握紧。His anger rose when the mechanic admitted using a second-hand part.
sceneCN: 这里 anger 是「愤怒、怒气」（第 1 个义项：因不公或受挫而生的强烈不快）；句意为修理工承认用了二手零件时，他的怒气升了上来。画面里有修车铺、坏掉的零件与握紧的拳头。

pos.zh: 名词：愤怒；怒气；义愤
动词：使发怒；激怒

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「生气的；愤怒的」
由 angry 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愤怒地」
由 angry 加 looking 构成的复合形容词，义为「面带怒色的」

senses.title: The feeling of anger
senses.definition: a strong feeling of displeasure and hostility caused by an injury, injustice or frustration
senses.definitionCN: 因受到伤害、不公或挫折而产生的强烈不快与敌意
senses.example: She felt a sudden anger at the unfairness of the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 这项决定的不公让她忽然感到愤怒。
senses.why: Old Norse angr meant grief and distress; anger is that tight, painful pressure turned outward.
senses.whyCN: 古诺尔斯语 angr 意为「悲伤、痛苦」；anger 就是那股收紧的痛感转而向外冲。

senses.title: An outburst or episode
senses.definition: a particular occasion or burst of angry feeling
senses.definitionCN: 某一次爆发出来的愤怒情绪
senses.example: He left the room in anger and slammed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他愤怒地离开房间，把门摔上。
senses.why: A mass noun can be counted when it comes in waves, so one surge of the feeling is an anger.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的情绪一旦成波涌来就能计数，于是一股涌起的怒气也可以说成一次 anger。

senses.title: To make someone angry
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel anger
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生愤怒
senses.example: The delays angered the passengers waiting on the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 延误激怒了在站台上等候的乘客。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction: instead of feeling the pressure, someone applies it to another.
senses.whyCN: 动词把方向反过来：不是自己承受那股压力，而是把它施加到别人身上。

senses.title: Anger at injustice
senses.definition: anger felt on moral grounds, especially at injustice done to others
senses.definitionCN: 出于道德理由产生的愤怒，尤指因他人遭受不公而愤怒
senses.example: Their anger at the pollution grew into a campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对污染的愤怒后来发展成一场运动。
senses.why: The same pressure rises when a wrong is witnessed, and society gives it a respectable name.
senses.whyCN: 目睹不公时同一股压力也会升起，社会给它一个体面的名字，叫义愤。

senses.title: The wrath of a god
senses.definition: in older and literary writing, the destructive displeasure of a god or fate
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文学作品中，指神或命运带有毁灭性的不悦
senses.example: The old story tells of the anger of the gods at human pride.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老故事讲述众神对人类傲慢的愤怒。
senses.why: Human anger writ large becomes a cosmic force, which is why wrath belongs to gods in epic writing.
senses.whyCN: 把人的愤怒放大，就成了宇宙级的力量，因此在史诗里「愤怒」属于神。

intro.en: Anger came from Old Norse, and its oldest sense is closer to grief than to rage.
intro.cn: anger 来自古诺尔斯语，它最早的义项更接近「悲痛」而不是「暴怒」。

items.en: The noun angr meant 'grief, sorrow, distress'. The emotional starting point is pain rather than attack.
items.cn: 名词 angr 意为「悲伤、痛苦、苦恼」，情感的起点是痛，而不是攻击。

items.en: The related verb angra meant 'to grieve, to vex', already close to causing distress.
items.cn: 相关动词 angra 意为「使悲伤、使烦恼」，已经接近「使人痛苦」。

items.en: The root *angh- is generally reconstructed as 'tight, painfully constricted'. It also underlies Latin angere and angustus. The reconstruction is not a recorded word.
items.cn: 词根 *angh- 一般重构为「紧绷、痛苦地收缩」，拉丁语 angere 与 angustus 也出自这里。该重构不是有记录的词。

items.en: Latin angere meant 'to choke, strangle, torment', and angustus meant 'narrow'. Both preserve the image of tightness.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angere 意为「使窒息、扼住、折磨」，angustus 意为「狭窄」，两者都保留了「紧绷」的意象。

items.en: English borrowed the Norse noun as anger; the exact first date is uncertain because early spellings differ.
items.cn: 英语把诺尔斯语名词借入为 anger；由于早期拼写不同，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun and verb settle into the modern pair, and the adjective angry grows from the noun with -y.
items.cn: 名词与动词固定为现代的一对，形容词 angry 由名词加 -y 长出。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tightness root; the near-meaning group ranks degrees of displeasure from irritation to wrath.
note.cn: 形近组共享「紧绷」词根；近义组按不快程度排列，从轻微恼怒到盛怒。

entries.definition: Adjective: feeling or showing anger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「生气的、愤怒的」，由本词加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Extreme pain or distress of mind; from Latin angustia, narrowness, the same tightness image.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「极度痛苦、苦恼」，来自拉丁语 angustia「狭窄」，共享同一个「紧绷」意象。

entries.definition: Worried and tense; from Latin anxius, built on the same choking root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑的、紧张的」，来自拉丁语 anxius，词根同样表示「收紧、窒息」。

entries.definition: A German borrowing for deep anxiety or dread, from the same Germanic family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焦虑、恐惧」，借自德语，与本词同属日耳曼语族。

entries.definition: Violent, uncontrolled anger; louder and less reasoned than anger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「暴怒」，比 anger 更失控、更外显。

entries.definition: Extremely strong anger, often compared to a storm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「狂怒」，愤怒极强，常被比作风暴。

entries.definition: Mild annoyance, much weaker than anger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恼怒、不耐烦」，程度远轻于 anger。

entries.definition: Formal or literary anger, especially the anger of a powerful figure or god.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「盛怒、天罚之怒」，属正式或文学用词，尤指强者或神的愤怒。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Norse grief word, the tightness root, and the family of Latin cognates.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的诺尔斯语「悲伤」词、表示「紧绷」的词根，以及拉丁同源词族。

normal.en: AnGR meant grief first; anger is grief that has turned hot and outward.
normal.cn: angr 最初是「悲伤」；anger 是转为灼热并向外冲的悲伤。

normal.en: Angere is to choke in Latin, angustus is narrow: the root image is a tightened throat.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 angere 是「扼住」，angustus 是「狭窄」：词根意象是收紧的喉咙。

normal.en: Angry adds -y to the noun; angrily adds -ly to the adjective.
normal.cn: angry 在名词后加 -y，angrily 在形容词后加 -ly。

normal.en: In anger is a fixed phrase for acting while the feeling is still hot.
normal.cn: in anger 是固定短语，指在怒气未消时行动。

normal.en: Righteous anger keeps the moral sense: the pressure rises at a wrong done to others.
normal.cn: righteous anger 保留道德义：这股压力因他人遭受不公而升起。

abstract.en: Picture a fist slowly closing around a small stone until the knuckles go white.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头慢慢握住一颗小石头，直到指节变白。

abstract.en: Picture steam building under a lid that shakes but has not yet lifted.
abstract.cn: 想象蒸气在锅盖下积聚，盖子震动却还没有被顶开。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow corridor that becomes narrower with every step, the walls pressing inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条越走越窄的走廊，两侧墙壁不断向内压来。

examples.en: His anger rose when the mechanic admitted using a second-hand part.
examples.cn: 修理工承认用了二手零件时，他的怒气升了上来。

examples.en: She felt a sudden anger at the unfairness of the decision.
examples.cn: 这项决定的不公让她忽然感到愤怒。

examples.en: The delays angered the passengers waiting on the platform.
examples.cn: 延误激怒了在站台上等候的乘客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂哥」——昂着头、脖子绷紧，一口气堵在胸口：愤怒、怒气

root: 古诺尔斯语名词 angr「悲伤、苦恼」与动词 angra「使苦恼」是直接来源，可追溯到一般重构为 *angh-「紧绷、痛苦地收缩」的印欧词根；拉丁语 angere「扼住、折磨」与 angustus「狭窄」同出此根。词义从「痛苦」转为向外爆发的「愤怒」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow one pressure: the feeling itself, one burst of it, the act of causing it, the moral version felt at injustice, and the literary version magnified into divine wrath.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项沿着同一股压力展开：情绪本身、一次爆发、施加于人的动作、面对不公时的道德版本，以及被放大成神怒的文学版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heat and pressure build behind the ribs until they force their way out through the voice.
core.cn: 核心意象：热与压力在肋骨后面积聚，最后从声音里冲出来。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: the steady state of displeasure and hostility.
branches.cn: 情绪线：持续存在的不快与敌意状态。

branches.en: THE EPISODE LINE: the feeling counted as one surge or occasion.
branches.cn: 发作线：把情绪数成一次涌起或一个场合。

branches.en: THE CAUSING LINE: the verb turns the pressure outward onto someone else.
branches.cn: 施加线：动词把压力转向外，施加到别人身上。

branches.en: THE JUSTICE LINE: the same pressure rises when a wrong is witnessed.
branches.cn: 正义线：目睹不公时，同一股压力也会升起。

branches.en: THE EPIC LINE: human anger magnified until it belongs to gods.
branches.cn: 史诗线：把人的愤怒放大，直到它属于神。

intro.en: Anger is a Norse noun with a Germanic root; English adds the ordinary adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: anger 是一个带日耳曼词根的诺尔斯语名词，英语再为它加上普通的形容词与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin angere, angustus and angor are genuine cognates through the reconstructed root, not borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 angere、angustus 与 angor 通过重构词根与它是真正的同源词，而不是借词。

sceneCN: 这里 angle 是「角、角度」（第 1 个义项：两条线或两个面相交形成的夹角）；句意为他用小角尺检查搁板与墙面之间的角度。画面里有靠墙的搁板、工匠与角尺。

pos.zh: 名词：角；角度；视角；倾斜；鱼钩（古旧义）
动词：钓鱼；斜行；从某一角度呈现

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 angulus 加 -ular 构成，义为「有角的；棱角分明的」
由 tri-「三」加 angle 构成，义为「三角形」
由 rect-「直」加 angle 构成，义为「长方形」
由钓鱼义的 angle 加 -er 构成，义为「钓鱼者」，这一支与几何义的 angle 词源不同

senses.title: The geometric angle
senses.definition: the figure formed by two lines or surfaces meeting at a point, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 两条线或两个面在同一点相交所形成的图形，用度数计量
senses.example: A right angle measures exactly ninety degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 直角正好是九十度。
senses.why: Latin angulus meant a corner: the place where two edges meet is the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angulus 意为「角、拐角」：两条边相交的那个地方就是最初的画面。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: the direction or standpoint from which a situation is considered
senses.definitionCN: 看待某种情形时所采取的方向或立场
senses.example: From a different angle, the whole dispute looks much simpler.
senses.exampleCN: 换一个角度看，整场争执显得简单多了。
senses.why: If a corner is where you stand, then changing corners means changing how things look.
senses.whyCN: 如果「角」是你站的位置，那么换一个角，就等于换一种看事物的结果。

senses.title: A slant or tilt
senses.definition: a position that is not flat or upright but leaning away from the vertical
senses.definitionCN: 不是水平或垂直，而是偏离竖直方向的位置
senses.example: The old roof sits at a steep angle above the street.
senses.exampleCN: 旧屋顶以很陡的倾斜度压在街道上方。
senses.why: Two surfaces that are not square to each other leave a visible angle between them.
senses.whyCN: 两个面若不彼此方正，中间就会留下看得见的夹角。

senses.title: To fish with a hook
senses.definition: to fish, especially with a rod and hook; also used figuratively for trying to obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 钓鱼，尤指用竿与钩；也比喻设法获取某物
senses.example: He angled for trout in the cold stream all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他一上午都在冰冷的溪流里钓鳟鱼。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word, Old English angel 'fishhook', and only shares the modern spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词，古英语 angel「鱼钩」，只是与几何义的 angle 共用今天的拼写。

senses.title: A fishhook
senses.definition: the older noun for a fishhook, now mainly historical
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的「鱼钩」名词义，今天主要出现在历史语境
senses.example: The fisherman lost his angle on a sunken branch.
senses.exampleCN: 渔夫的鱼钩挂在一根沉在水下的树枝上，丢了。
senses.why: Before the geometry word crowded it out, angle named the hooked tool itself.
senses.whyCN: 在几何义把这个词占满之前，angle 指的就是那个带钩的工具本身。

senses.title: A corner or street corner
senses.definition: an older use for a corner of a building or the meeting point of two streets
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指建筑的拐角或两条街道相交处
senses.example: They met at the angle of the two streets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在两条街相交的拐角处见面。
senses.why: This keeps the Latin corner sense in its most literal, physical form.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语「拐角」义最字面、最具体的保留。

intro.en: Angle is two different words that became one spelling: a Latin corner word and an Old English hook word.
intro.cn: angle 其实是两个不同的词合并成同一个拼写：一个来自拉丁语的「拐角」，一个来自古英语的「鱼钩」。

items.en: Angulus meant 'a corner, an angle'. It is the source of the geometric family and has no connection with fishhooks.
items.cn: angulus 意为「拐角、角」，是几何这一族的来源，与鱼钩毫无关系。

items.en: A separate word, angel, meant 'fishhook'. It belongs to a different root meaning 'hook, bend'.
items.cn: 另一个独立的词 angel 意为「鱼钩」，属于表示「钩、弯」的不同词根。

items.en: The geometric sense enters English through French, and angle begins to name corners and the space between meeting lines.
items.cn: 几何义经法语进入英语，angle 开始指拐角以及相交线之间的空间。

items.en: The fishing verb and noun continue alongside the geometric word, and the two spellings merge.
items.cn: 钓鱼的动词与名词与几何词并行发展，两者的拼写最终合一。

items.en: Geometry keeps angle and angular, while fishing keeps angler; the shared spelling hides two separate histories.
items.cn: 几何保留 angle 与 angular，钓鱼保留 angler；共同的拼写掩盖了两条彼此独立的历史。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes the corner family with the fishing word; the near-meaning group gathers corners and standpoints.
note.cn: 形近组把「拐角」一族与钓鱼词放在一起；近义组收拐角与立场类词。

entries.definition: Having angles or sharp corners; from Latin angulus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有角的、棱角分明的」，来自拉丁语 angulus。

entries.definition: A flat shape with three straight sides, literally three angles.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「三角形」，字面就是「三个角」。

entries.definition: A four-sided shape with right angles, literally a right angle shape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长方形」，字面是「直角形」。

entries.definition: A person who fishes with a hook; this word comes from the Old English fishhook root, not from angulus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钓鱼者」，来自古英语「鱼钩」词根，并非来自拉丁语 angulus。

entries.definition: The point where two edges or streets meet; the plain everyday word for the Latin sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「角、拐角」，是拉丁语「角」义最日常的说法。

entries.definition: A way of looking at a matter, closer to the figurative angle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观点、立场」，接近 angle 的比喻义。

entries.definition: A particular way of judging things based on one's position or experience.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视角、看法」，指基于位置或经验形成的判断方式。

entries.definition: A curve or turn in a road or line, not a measured angle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「弯曲、转弯」，指道路或线条的转向，不是可度量的角。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the two real origins apart and attach them to the families they actually produced.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把两个真实来源分开，并各自挂到它们实际产生的词族上。

normal.en: Angulus is a corner: two edges meet and leave a measurable opening.
normal.cn: angulus 是「拐角」：两条边相交，留下一个可度量的开口。

normal.en: Old English angel is a fishhook: a different word that happens to share the modern spelling.
normal.cn: 古英语 angel 是「鱼钩」：另一个词，只是碰巧与今天的拼写相同。

normal.en: Triangle and rectangle are literally three-angle and right-angle shapes.
normal.cn: triangle 与 rectangle 字面就是「三个角」与「直角」的形状。

normal.en: Angler belongs to fishing, not geometry; its -er marks the person, not the corner.
normal.cn: angler 属于钓鱼而不是几何；它的 -er 标出的是人，不是角。

normal.en: From a different angle is the fixed phrase for a change of standpoint.
normal.cn: from a different angle 是表示「换立场」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture two roads leaving one crossroads, the space between them opening wider as they go.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路从同一个十字路口分开，越走中间的空隙越大。

abstract.en: Picture a camera moved one step to the side: the same room, a different story.
abstract.cn: 想象摄影机往旁边挪了一步：同一个房间，讲出了不同的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a hook under water, curved like a bent corner, waiting for a pull.
abstract.cn: 想象水下一只钩子，弯得像一个折角，等着被拉动。

examples.en: He checked the angle between the shelf and the wall with a small square tool.
examples.cn: 他用小角尺检查搁板与墙面之间的角度。

examples.en: From a different angle, the whole dispute looks much simpler.
examples.cn: 换一个角度看，整场争执显得简单多了。

examples.en: He angled for trout in the cold stream all morning.
examples.cn: 他一上午都在冰冷的溪流里钓鳟鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺够」——俺够了够墙角那个角度，又拿钩子去钓鱼：角、钓鱼

root: 几何义来自拉丁语 angulus「拐角、角」，经法语进入英语；钓鱼义来自古英语 angel「鱼钩」，属于表示「钩、弯」的另一词根。两词在现代英语中拼写合一，但历史彼此独立，不能混为一条词源。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses divide into two histories: four belong to the corner word, including the figurative standpoint, and two belong to the fishhook word.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项分成两条历史：四个属于「拐角」词，包括比喻的立场义；两个属于「鱼钩」词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines leave one point and open a measurable gap between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条线从同一点出发，中间张开一个可度量的口。

branches.en: THE GEOMETRY LINE: the measured opening between two meeting lines.
branches.cn: 几何线：两条相交线之间可度量的开口。

branches.en: THE VIEW LINE: a standpoint treated as a corner you stand in.
branches.cn: 视角线：把立场当作你站立的那个角。

branches.en: THE TILT LINE: surfaces out of square leave a visible angle.
branches.cn: 倾斜线：不方正的两个面之间留下看得见的夹角。

branches.en: THE CORNER LINE: the oldest physical sense, a corner of a building or street.
branches.cn: 拐角线：最古老的具体义，建筑或街道的拐角。

branches.en: THE HOOK LINE: a separate Old English word for fishing and the fishhook itself.
branches.cn: 钩线：来自另一个古英语词，指钓鱼与鱼钩本身。

intro.en: The geometric angle is built on Latin angulus; the fishing angle belongs to a separate Old English hook word.
intro.cn: 几何义的 angle 建在拉丁语 angulus 上；钓鱼义的 angle 属于另一个古英语「钩」词。

latinIntro.en: Latin angulus and its adjective angularis are recorded, and triangulus is a documented compound; none of these is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 angulus 及其形容词 angularis 都有记录，triangulus 也是有文献的复合词，均非重构。

items.exampleCN: 它是几何词族的来源。

items.example: It appears in angular and angularity.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 angular 与 angularity 中。

items.example: It forms angular.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 angular。

items.example: It forms triangle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 triangle。

items.example: It forms rectangle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 rectangle。

items.example: It is the separate source of the fishing sense.
items.exampleCN: 它是钓鱼义的另一个来源。

items.example: It forms angler from the fishing verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把钓鱼动词构成 angler。

items.example: It forms angled.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 angled。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 angulus 加形容词后缀构成，义为「有角的；棱角分明的」
由 tri-「三」加 angle 构成，义为「三角形」
由钓鱼义的 angle 加 -er 构成，义为「钓鱼者」，与几何义不同源

definition_zh: 生气的；愤怒的；怒容的；汹涌险恶的；（伤口）发炎的
definition_en: feeling or showing strong displeasure; also used of storms, seas or infected wounds
core_image: 脸一下涨红，下颌咬紧，话从牙缝里出来
scene: 公交车上，有人把湿伞甩到旁边乘客的裤腿上，连一句道歉也没有。The passenger gave an angry look at the man with the dripping umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里 angry 是「愤怒的、带怒色的」（第 2 个义项：把怒气表现在表情上）；句意为那位乘客朝拿湿伞的人投去愤怒的一眼。画面里有公交车、湿伞与乘客的怒色。

pos.zh: 形容词：生气的；愤怒的；怒容的；汹涌的；（伤口）发炎的

derivatives.zh: 本词的名词形式，义为「愤怒；怒气」，与本词同出古诺尔斯语 angr
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愤怒地」

senses.title: Feeling anger
senses.definition: feeling strong displeasure, especially because of an injury, injustice or frustration
senses.definitionCN: 因受到伤害、不公或挫折而感到强烈不快
senses.example: She was angry with her brother for losing the keys again.
senses.exampleCN: 弟弟又把钥匙弄丢了，她对他很生气。
senses.why: The adjective adds -y to anger, so it names a person filled with that tight, hot pressure.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由 anger 加 -y 构成，因此它命名的是被那股紧绷热压充满的人。

senses.title: Showing anger
senses.titleCN: 带怒色的；表现出愤怒的
senses.definition: used of looks, words or faces that clearly express anger
senses.definitionCN: 用于清楚表现出愤怒的眼神、言辞或面孔
senses.example: The passenger gave an angry look at the man with the dripping umbrella.
senses.exampleCN: 那位乘客朝拿湿伞的人投去愤怒的一眼。
senses.why: What a person feels inside becomes visible outside, and the adjective moves from the feeling to its signs.
senses.whyCN: 人心里感受到的东西会显到外面，于是这个形容词从「感受」转到了「表现」。

senses.title: Violent or threatening, as of weather
senses.definition: used in literary writing of a sea, sky or storm that seems violently hostile
senses.definitionCN: 文学用语，形容海、天空或风暴仿佛带着猛烈的敌意
senses.example: The angry sea threw white water over the harbour wall.
senses.exampleCN: 汹涌的大海把白浪抛过港湾的堤墙。
senses.why: Nature has no temper, but a violent storm looks like a person in a rage, so the human word is lent to it.
senses.whyCN: 自然并没有脾气，但猛烈的风暴看上去像人在暴怒，于是把人的词借给了它。

senses.title: Inflamed, as of a wound
senses.definition: used informally of a cut or wound that is red, sore and infected
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指伤口发红、疼痛并有感染
senses.example: The cut on his knee looked angry and needed cleaning.
senses.exampleCN: 他膝上的伤口看起来发炎了，需要清理。
senses.why: Red, hot, swollen flesh looks the way anger feels, so the same word covers bodily inflammation.
senses.whyCN: 发红、发热、肿起的皮肉，看起来就像愤怒的感觉，于是同一个词也覆盖身体的炎症。

intro.en: Angry is the adjective built on the Norse noun anger, and its history is the history of that pressure.
intro.cn: angry 是建在诺尔斯语名词 anger 上的形容词，它的历史就是那股压力的历史。

items.en: The noun angr meant grief and distress; the emotional starting point was pain rather than attack.
items.cn: 名词 angr 意为「悲伤、痛苦」，情感起点是痛，而不是攻击。

items.en: English borrowed the noun as anger, and it gradually narrowed toward hot displeasure.
items.cn: 英语把名词借入为 anger，词义逐渐收窄为灼热的不快。

items.en: The adjective angry appears with the ending -y, meaning 'full of anger'. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 angry 以 -y 词尾出现，意为「充满怒气的」；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word extends to faces, words and storms, lending human temper to things that have none.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到面孔、言辞与风暴，把人的脾气借给本无脾气的事物。

items.en: The informal medical use for inflamed wounds settles in, alongside the fixed frames angry with, angry at and angry about.
items.cn: 指伤口发炎的口语用法固定下来，同时形成 angry with、angry at、angry about 等固定搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same anger family; the near-meaning group ranks the strength of displeasure.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个 anger 词族；近义组按不快程度排列。

entries.definition: The noun and verb for the feeling and for causing it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词与动词，指愤怒这种情绪以及使人生怒的动作。

entries.definition: Adverb: in an angry manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「愤怒地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Past participle of the verb anger: made angry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 anger 的过去分词，义为「被激怒的」。

entries.definition: Extremely angry, far stronger than angry.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「暴怒的」，程度远强于 angry。

entries.definition: Mildly angry, usually about a small repeated irritation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恼火的」，程度较轻，多因反复的小麻烦而起。

entries.definition: Informal for very angry; in British English it can also mean insane.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，口语中义为「非常生气」，在英式英语里也可指「发疯的」。

entries.definition: Mildly angry, especially in British informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有点生气的」，多见于英式口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Norse source, the -y ending, and the frames that decide which preposition follows.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的诺尔斯语来源、-y 词尾，以及决定后面接哪个介词的句式。

normal.en: Angr was grief; angry is that grief heated up and pushed outward.
normal.cn: angr 是悲伤；angry 是那份悲伤被加热后向外推。

normal.en: Add -y to anger and you get angry, the way a person is filled with the feeling.
normal.cn: anger 加 -y 就得 angry，表示一个人被这种情绪充满。

normal.en: Angry with a person, angry at a thing or action, angry about a situation.
normal.cn: 对人生气用 angry with，对行为或事物用 angry at，对情形用 angry about。

normal.en: The angry sea and the angry wound both borrow the human heat for something without a temper.
normal.cn: angry sea 与 angry wound 都是把人的热度借给本无脾气的东西。

normal.en: Angrier and angriest change the y to i before the ending, like happy and happier.
normal.cn: angrier 与 angriest 在词尾前把 y 变 i，正如 happy 变 happier。

abstract.en: Picture a face going red from the collar upward, the jaw locking before any word comes out.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸从衣领往上红起来，下颌先咬紧，话还没出口。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle left on the fire, the lid rattling harder and harder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水壶留在火上，壶盖越响越急。

abstract.en: Picture a wound drawing a red circle around itself, hot to the touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一处伤口在周围画出一圈红色，摸上去发烫。

examples.en: The passenger gave an angry look at the man with the dripping umbrella.
examples.cn: 那位乘客朝拿湿伞的人投去愤怒的一眼。

examples.en: She was angry with her brother for losing the keys again.
examples.cn: 弟弟又把钥匙弄丢了，她对他很生气。

examples.en: The cut on his knee looked angry and needed cleaning.
examples.cn: 他膝上的伤口看起来发炎了，需要清理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂格瑞」——昂着头、格开别人、锐气冲冲：生气的

root: 古诺尔斯语名词 angr「悲伤、苦恼」经英语借入为 anger，再加形容词后缀 -y 构成 angry，义为「充满怒气的」。词根可追溯到一般重构为 *angh-「紧绷、收缩」的印欧词根，与拉丁语 angere「扼住」、angustus「狭窄」同源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses spread one heat outward: a person feeling it, a face showing it, a storm behaving like it, and a wound burning with it.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项把同一股热向外扩散：感受它的人、表现它的面孔、像它一样发作的风暴，以及带着它发烫的伤口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heat rises into the face, the jaw locks, and the feeling becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：热升到脸上，下颌咬紧，情绪变得看得见。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: a person filled with strong displeasure.
branches.cn: 感受线：一个人被强烈的不快充满。

branches.en: THE SIGN LINE: the feeling becomes visible in looks and words.
branches.cn: 表现线：情绪在眼神与言辞里变得看得见。

branches.en: THE WEATHER LINE: a violent sea or sky acts like an angry person.
branches.cn: 天气线：汹涌的海或天空表现得像发怒的人。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: red, hot, swollen flesh borrows the same image.
branches.cn: 身体线：发红、发热、肿起的皮肉借用同一个意象。

branches.en: THE HEAT LINE: the feeling and the inflammation are two ends of the same inner heat.
branches.cn: 热度线：情绪与炎症是同一股内在热量的两端。

intro.en: Angry is anger plus the adjective ending -y; its relatives come from the same Norse and Germanic root.
intro.cn: angry 是 anger 加形容词词尾 -y；它的亲属词来自同一个诺尔斯语与日耳曼语词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin angere and angustus are genuine cognates through the reconstructed root, not borrowings into English.

definition_en: a living creature that can move and feed, as opposed to a plant; also the bodily or instinctive side of human nature
core_image: 一只有呼吸、会动、会回看你的生命，与石头和机器不同
scene: 雨后的草地上，一只小鹿从树影里探出头，耳朵轻轻转动。The animal froze when it heard the gate open.
sceneCN: 这里 animal 是「动物」（第 1 个义项：能活动、能进食的生物）；句意为那只动物听见院门打开就僵住不动。画面里有雨后草地、树影与小鹿。

pos.zh: 名词：动物；兽；牲畜；粗暴的人
形容词：动物的；肉体的；本能的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 anima「呼吸、灵魂」派生，义为「使有生气；有生命的」，与本词同出一词根

senses.title: A living creature that moves
senses.definition: a living thing that can move, feed and respond to its surroundings, as distinct from a plant
senses.definitionCN: 能活动、进食并对周围作出反应的生命，与植物相对
senses.example: Every animal in the forest depends on the same river.
senses.exampleCN: 森林里的每一种动物都依赖同一条河。
senses.why: Latin animal came from anima, breath or soul: the moving, breathing thing is the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 animal 来自 anima「呼吸、灵魂」：会动、会呼吸的东西就是最初的含义。

senses.title: A beast, especially a mammal
senses.definition: in everyday use, a four-legged creature, especially a mammal, rather than a bird or insect
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中，尤指四足哺乳动物，而不是鸟或昆虫
senses.example: The zoo keeps large animals in open enclosures.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园把大型动物养在开阔的围栏里。
senses.why: The general category narrows in daily speech to the creatures people most often picture.
senses.whyCN: 在日常说话中，这个总类收窄成人们最容易想到的那些生物。

senses.title: Livestock
senses.definition: farm creatures kept for work, milk, meat or wool
senses.definitionCN: 为劳作、产奶、取肉或取毛而饲养的农家动物
senses.example: The farm animals were moved to higher ground before the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水来临前，农场的牲畜被赶到了高处。
senses.why: A working farm turns the category into property, and farm animal becomes a standard unit of farming.
senses.whyCN: 经营性农场把这个类别变成了财产，farm animal 于是成为农业里的标准单位。

senses.title: A brutal person
senses.definition: a person who behaves in a crude, violent or unfeeling way
senses.definitionCN: 行为粗野、暴力或没有同情心的人
senses.example: He behaved like an animal and shouted at the waiter.
senses.exampleCN: 他像畜生一样，对服务员大吼大叫。
senses.why: Calling a person an animal denies the human qualities of reason and care, reducing them to mere appetite.
senses.whyCN: 把人称作 animal，就是否认其理性与关怀，把人降成只有欲望的东西。

senses.title: Bodily or instinctive
senses.definition: used as an adjective for the physical, instinctive side of human nature
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指人性中属于身体与本能的层面
senses.example: Animal instincts kept the herd together in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 本能的力量让兽群在风暴中聚在一起。
senses.why: If an animal is the part of us that breathes and reacts, the adjective names that part directly.
senses.whyCN: 如果动物就是我们身上会呼吸、会反应的那部分，那么形容词就直接命名这一部分。

intro.en: Animal is Latin for a breathing being; the breath became the soul, and the soul became a category of life.
intro.cn: animal 在拉丁语里指「会呼吸的存在」；呼吸变成灵魂，灵魂又变成生命的一个类别。

items.en: Anima meant 'breath, air, soul'. Breathing was the clearest sign that something was alive.
items.cn: anima 意为「呼吸、气息、灵魂」，呼吸是某物活着最清楚的标志。

items.en: Animal was a noun formed from anima, meaning 'a living being, a breathing creature'.
items.cn: animal 是由 anima 构成的名词，意为「活物、会呼吸的生物」。

items.en: The adjective animalis meant 'of a living being, breathing, animate'.
items.cn: 形容词 animalis 意为「有生命的、会呼吸的、有生气的」。

items.en: Old French animal carried the noun into everyday use before it reached English.
items.cn: 古法语 animal 把这个名词带入日常使用，随后进入英语。

items.en: English borrowed animal as a general word for living creatures; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入 animal 作为泛指生物的普通词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Science narrows the word to non-plant life, while everyday speech adds livestock, beasts and the human body senses.
items.cn: 科学把这个词收窄为「非植物的生命」，日常语言又加入牲畜、野兽与人体本能等义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the breath-and-soul family; the near-meaning group gathers living creatures by scale and type.
note.cn: 形近组收「呼吸与灵魂」词族；近义组按大小与类型收各类生物词。

entries.definition: To give life or energy to; also an adjective meaning living.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使有生气、赋予生命」，也可作形容词指「有生命的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: The state of being full of life, or the technique of making drawings move.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生气、活力」或「动画」，指使画面动起来的技术。

entries.definition: The belief that natural objects and places have souls.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「万物有灵论」，相信自然物与地点拥有灵魂。

entries.definition: A person who gives life to drawings or puppets.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「动画制作者」，指让图画或木偶动起来的人。

entries.definition: Any living being, often one that is small, strange or unknown.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生物、造物」，常指较小、奇特或未知的生命。

entries.definition: A large or dangerous four-legged animal; stronger and older in tone than animal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「野兽」，指大型或危险的走兽，语气比 animal 更古、更重。

entries.definition: A warm-blooded animal that feeds its young on milk; a scientific subcategory.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「哺乳动物」，指温血、以乳汁哺育幼崽的动物，是科学分类下的子类。

entries.definition: Animals and plants living free in nature, treated as a collective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「野生动植物」，指在自然中自由生活的动植物整体。

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「呼吸」词，以及它产生的科学与日常用法。

normal.en: Anima is breath: an animal is first of all the thing that breathes and moves.
normal.cn: anima 是呼吸：animal 首先就是会呼吸、会动的东西。

normal.en: Animate gives breath to a drawing; animation is the result.
normal.cn: animate 是给图画「吹气」，animation 就是吹气后的结果。

normal.en: Farm animals are livestock, the category turned into property.
normal.cn: farm animals 是牲畜，类别变成了财产。

normal.en: Calling a person an animal strips away reason and care, leaving only appetite.
normal.cn: 把人称作 animal，就是剥去理性与关怀，只剩下欲望。

normal.en: Animal instincts is the adjective use: the bodily, instinctive part of a person.
normal.cn: animal instincts 是形容词用法，指人身上属于身体与本能的部位。

abstract.en: Picture a deer's ears turning before its body moves, the whole animal listening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹿的耳朵先转动，身体还没动，整只动物都在听。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on paper suddenly given breath and stepping off the page.
abstract.cn: 想象纸上的一条线忽然被吹进一口气，从页面里走出来。

abstract.en: Picture two sides inside one person, one reasoning and one breathing hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人体内有两面，一面讲理，一面喘着粗气。

examples.cn: 那只动物听见院门打开就僵住不动。

root: 拉丁语 anima「呼吸、气息、灵魂」是词根，由其构成名词 animal「活物、会呼吸的生物」与形容词 animalis「有生命的」。经古法语 animal 进入英语，先泛指生物，现代科学收窄为「非植物的生命」，日常又衍生牲畜、野兽与人体本能等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from the breathing creature to the beast, the livestock, the brutal person, and the instinctive side of a human being.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从会呼吸的生物，走到兽、牲畜、粗暴的人，以及人身上属于本能的那一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a breathing creature turns its ears toward a sound and moves before thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只会呼吸的生物把耳朵转向声音，先动起来再思考。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY LINE: any living, moving thing that is not a plant.
branches.cn: 类别线：任何会动、会呼吸且不是植物的生命。

branches.en: THE BEAST LINE: the everyday narrowing to four-legged mammals.
branches.cn: 野兽线：日常语言收窄到四足哺乳动物。

branches.en: THE FARM LINE: the same category turned into property and work.
branches.cn: 农场线：同一类别变成财产与劳力。

branches.en: THE INSULT LINE: a person reduced to appetite without reason.
branches.cn: 贬义线：把人降成没有理性的欲望。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: the adjective names the instinctive side of a human being.
branches.cn: 身体线：形容词命名人身上属于本能的一面。

definition_zh: 宣布；公布；通报；播报；预示；正式告知
definition_en: to make a piece of information known publicly or officially, especially in a formal or deliberate way
core_image: 一个人站到众人面前，把消息清楚地大声说出来
scene: 学校礼堂里，校长走上台，手里拿着一张名单，台下安静下来。The head teacher announced the winner of the writing prize.
sceneCN: 这里 announced 是「宣布」（第 1 个义项：把消息公开、正式地讲出来）；句意为校长宣布了写作奖的得主。画面里有礼堂、拿着名单的校长与安静的台下。

pos.zh: 动词：宣布；公布；通报；播报；预示

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「公告；宣布」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「播音员；报幕员」
过去分词作形容词，义为「已宣布的；公开表明的」

senses.title: To make something known publicly
senses.definition: to tell a piece of news or a decision to a group of people in a formal, deliberate way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式、刻意的方式把一条消息或决定告诉一群人
senses.example: The company announced a new plant in the north of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 公司宣布将在城市北部新建一座工厂。
senses.why: Latin annuntiare is to bring a message: the verb puts a messenger's report in front of an audience.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annuntiare 是「把消息带来」：这个动词把传信人的报告摆到听众面前。

senses.title: To announce a visitor
senses.definition: to tell people that a guest has arrived, especially in a formal household or event
senses.definitionCN: 告知有人到来，尤用于正式家庭或场合
senses.example: The butler announced the arrival of the evening guests.
senses.exampleCN: 管家通报了晚宴客人的到来。
senses.why: A name spoken at the door turns an arrival into an official event, which is the message-bringing sense in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 在门口报出一个名字，就把「到达」变成正式事件，这正是「传消息」义的小型版本。

senses.title: To read out over radio or television
senses.definition: to read information aloud to an audience, as a broadcaster or programme presenter does
senses.definitionCN: 像播音员或节目主持人那样，把信息向听众或观众朗读出来
senses.example: The radio station announced the storm warning at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 电台在中午播报了风暴警报。
senses.why: Broadcasting keeps the messenger but changes the room: the audience is now scattered across many homes.
senses.whyCN: 广播保留了传信人，却换了房间：听众现在分散在许多家庭里。

senses.title: To be a sign of something
senses.definition: to make something clear in advance, as a sign or result does
senses.definitionCN: 像迹象或结果那样，预先使某事变得清楚
senses.example: The early flowers announced the arrival of spring.
senses.exampleCN: 早开的花预示着春天的到来。
senses.why: A sign delivers a message without a speaker, so the verb extends from people to things.
senses.whyCN: 迹象没有说话人也能送出消息，于是这个动词从人扩展到事物。

senses.title: To make a formal personal announcement
senses.definition: to state family news such as a birth, engagement or death in a formal notice
senses.definitionCN: 以正式启事的形式公布出生、订婚或去世等家庭消息
senses.example: They announced the birth of their daughter in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在当地报纸上公布了女儿出生的消息。
senses.why: Private news becomes public through a fixed social form, and the verb names that form.
senses.whyCN: 私人的消息通过一种固定的社会形式公开，这个动词命名的正是那种形式。

intro.en: Announce is built from a Latin messenger word; the message travels through French before it reaches English.
intro.cn: announce 由一个拉丁语「传信人」词构成；消息先经法语，再抵达英语。

items.en: Nuntius meant 'messenger' and also 'message'. It is the person-and-news word at the centre of the family.
items.cn: nuntius 意为「传信人」，也指「消息」，是这一词族中心那个兼指人与消息的词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus nuntiare 'to bring news' formed annuntiare, 'to announce, to report'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad-「向」加 nuntiare「带来消息」构成 annuntiare，意为「宣布、报告」。

items.en: Old French anoncier carried the verb into the language of court and town, with the sense of formally making news known.
items.cn: 古法语 anoncier 把这个动词带入宫廷与城镇语言，义为正式地把消息公开。

items.en: English borrowed the French verb as announce; the exact first date is uncertain because spellings vary.
items.cn: 英语把法语动词借入为 announce；由于拼写不一，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Broadcasting, public relations and family notices each add a distinct setting for the same messenger.
items.cn: 广播、公共关系与家庭启事各自为同一个「传信人」增加了不同的场景。

note.en: The look-alike group is the message family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of making news public with different levels of formality.
note.cn: 形近组收「消息」词族；近义组收把消息公开的动词，正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or the text of announcing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宣布；公告」，指宣布的动作或文本。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to read information aloud to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「播音员、报幕员」，指以朗读信息为职业的人。

entries.definition: Past participle used as an adjective: made known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，义为「已宣布的、公开表明的」。

entries.definition: To state something officially and firmly, often ending doubt or dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣告、声明」，正式而坚定，常用来终结疑问或争议。

entries.definition: To announce something publicly with ceremony or authority; grander than announce.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣告、公告」，带仪式感或权威色彩，比 announce 更宏大。

entries.definition: To make previously hidden information visible; the emphasis is on disclosure, not publicity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「揭示、透露」，强调把原本隐藏的信息公开，而不是面向公众发布。

entries.definition: To make something known in order to attract attention or sales.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「做广告、宣传」，公开的目的是吸引注意或促进销售。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin messenger word and the settings where the verb now works.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「传信人」词，以及这个动词今天工作的场景。

normal.en: Nuntius is messenger: announce is to put the messenger in front of the room.
normal.cn: nuntius 是传信人：announce 就是把传信人放到整个房间面前。

normal.en: Ad- plus nuntiare: bring the news to someone, not just have it.
normal.cn: ad- 加 nuntiare：把消息带到某人那里，而不是只握在手里。

normal.en: Announcement is the text; announcer is the person; announced is the state.
normal.cn: announcement 是文本，announcer 是人，announced 是状态。

normal.en: A sign can announce spring: the messenger does not need a voice.
normal.cn: 迹象也能 announce 春天：传信人不一定需要嗓子。

normal.en: Birth announcements in a paper turn private news into a public form.
normal.cn: 报纸上的出生启事把私人消息变成公开形式。

abstract.en: Picture a person stepping onto a low stage, one sheet of paper in hand, the room going quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走上矮台，手里拿着一张纸，整个房间安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a door opening before the knock ends, the name spoken into the hall.
abstract.cn: 想象敲门声还没落，门已打开，名字被报进大厅。

abstract.en: Picture a messenger running along a road, the news arriving before the person does.
abstract.cn: 想象传信人沿路奔跑，消息比人先到。

examples.cn: 校长宣布了写作奖的得主。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额闹恩斯」——额头上冒汗、闹哄哄地恩斯一声把消息喊出来：宣布

root: 拉丁语 nuntius「传信人、消息」加前缀 ad-「向」构成动词 annuntiare「宣布、报告」，经古法语 anoncier 进入英语为 announce。词义始终围绕「把消息带到公众面前」，现代扩展出播报、预示与报刊启事等场景。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow one messenger: before a crowd, at a door, over the air, through a sign, and inside a formal family notice.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项跟着同一个传信人：站在人群前、站在门口、通过广播、借迹象传达，以及出现在正式的家庭启事里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a messenger stands before a room and states the news so that everyone hears it at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：传信人站在一屋子人面前说出消息，让所有人同时听到。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC LINE: a decision or piece of news is placed before a group.
branches.cn: 公开线：把决定或消息摆到一群人的面前。

branches.en: THE DOOR LINE: a name spoken at the entrance turns an arrival into an event.
branches.cn: 门口线：在入口处报出名字，把「到达」变成事件。

branches.en: THE AIR LINE: the messenger speaks through radio or television to scattered listeners.
branches.cn: 广播线：传信人通过电台或电视，对分散的听众说话。

branches.en: THE SIGN LINE: a thing without a voice still delivers its message.
branches.cn: 迹象线：没有嗓子的事物也能送出消息。

branches.en: THE NOTICE LINE: private family news takes a fixed public form.
branches.cn: 启事线：私人的家庭消息采用固定的公开形式。

intro.en: Announce joins a Latin prefix of direction to the messenger word, and English adds ordinary noun and person endings.
intro.cn: announce 把表示方向的拉丁前缀接到「传信人」一词上，英语再加普通的指物与指人词尾。

latinIntro.en: Nuntius, nuntiare and annuntiare are recorded Latin words, so nothing in this word is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: nuntius、nuntiare 与 annuntiare 都是有记录的拉丁词，因此这个词里没有重构形式。

definition_zh: 公告；通告；宣布；启事；广播通知
definition_en: a formal public statement or notice that makes information known to a group of people
core_image: 一张贴到公告栏上的纸，路过的人都停下来读
scene: 车站大厅的广播忽然响起，所有人抬头看向上方的屏幕。A loud announcement told passengers that the last train would leave from platform two.
sceneCN: 这里 announcement 是「广播通知」（第 1 个义项：面向公众发布的正式消息）；句意为一则响亮的广播通知告知乘客，末班车将从二号站台开出。画面里有车站大厅、仰头的人群与上方的屏幕。

pos.zh: 名词：公告；通告；宣布；启事；广播通知

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「宣布；公布」，由拉丁语 annuntiare 经法语进入英语
由 announce 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「播音员；报幕员」
由 announce 加过去分词后缀构成，义为「已宣布的；公开表明的」

senses.title: A formal public notice
senses.definition: a formal statement or notice that gives information to a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 向一群人提供信息的正式声明或告示
senses.example: The school posted an announcement about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 学校贴出了关于新课程表的公告。
senses.why: Announce plus -ment turns the act of bringing news into the thing that carries the news.
senses.whyCN: announce 加 -ment，把「带消息」的动作变成了承载消息的那个东西。

senses.title: The act of announcing
senses.definition: the act or occasion of making something known, especially when it surprises people
senses.definitionCN: 把某事公开的动作或场合，尤指使人意外的宣布
senses.example: His announcement surprised the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他的宣布让整个委员会都很意外。
senses.why: The suffix -ment can name the action itself as well as its result, so one word covers both.
senses.whyCN: -ment 既能命名动作本身，也能命名动作的结果，因此同一个词兼具两义。

senses.title: A small advertisement or notice
senses.definition: a short notice placed in a newspaper or on a board, often advertising a job or service
senses.definitionCN: 登在报纸或贴在告示板上的短启事，常用于招聘或服务信息
senses.example: She found the job in the announcements at the back of the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她在报纸后面的启事栏里找到了这份工作。
senses.why: A paid notice is still a public message, and the newspaper simply becomes the room it is read in.
senses.whyCN: 付费启事仍然是公开消息，只是报纸变成了它被读到的那间「房间」。

senses.title: A birth, marriage or death notice
senses.definition: a formal family notice in a newspaper recording a birth, engagement, marriage or death
senses.definitionCN: 登在报纸上的正式家庭启事，公布出生、订婚、结婚或去世
senses.example: They placed a birth announcement in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在当地报纸上登了一则出生启事。
senses.why: Private news is given a fixed public form, and that form takes the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 私人的消息被赋予一个固定的公开形式，这个形式就沿用了「宣布」的名字。

senses.title: A spoken broadcast notice
senses.definition: a message read aloud over a public address system, radio or television
senses.definitionCN: 通过公共广播、电台或电视朗读出来的通知
senses.example: A loud announcement told passengers that the last train would leave from platform two.
senses.exampleCN: 一则响亮的广播通知告知乘客，末班车将从二号站台开出。
senses.why: The audience is scattered but the message arrives at once, which is why broadcasting keeps this word.
senses.whyCN: 听众是分散的，消息却同时抵达，因此广播场景一直沿用这个词。

intro.en: Announcement is the noun built on announce, whose Latin core is a messenger bringing news.
intro.cn: announcement 是建在 announce 上的名词，其拉丁核心是一个带来消息的传信人。

items.en: Nuntius meant 'messenger' and 'message'; the word carries both the bearer and the thing carried.
items.cn: nuntius 兼指「传信人」与「消息」，这个词同时带着送信的人与被送的内容。

items.en: Annuntiare meant 'to bring news to someone, to report', built with ad- 'to' plus nuntiare.
items.cn: annuntiare 意为「把消息带给某人、报告」，由 ad-「向」加 nuntiare 构成。

items.en: Old French anoncier and the noun anonce carried the meaning into the everyday language of courts and towns.
items.cn: 古法语动词 anoncier 与名词 anonce 把这个意思带进宫廷与城镇的日常语言。

items.en: English took the verb announce and formed the noun with -ment; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入动词 announce，并用 -ment 造出名词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun spreads into public administration, newspapers, broadcasting and family notices.
items.cn: 这个名词扩展到公共行政、报纸、广播与家庭启事。

note.en: The look-alike group is the announce family; the near-meaning group gathers public statements of different length and formality.
note.cn: 形近组收 announce 词族；近义组收各类公开声明，篇幅与正式程度不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make information known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布；公布」，指把信息向公众公开。

entries.definition: A person who reads announcements aloud, on radio or at an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「播音员、报幕员」，指在电台或活动现场朗读通知的人。

entries.definition: Past participle used as an adjective: made known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，义为「已宣布的、公开表明的」。

entries.definition: A written or printed sign giving information; shorter and less formal than an announcement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通知、告示」，指书面或印刷的信息，比 announcement 更短、更不正式。

entries.definition: A formal account of facts or a position, often issued by an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「声明、陈述」，指对事实或立场的正式说明，常由机构发布。

entries.definition: A solemn or official statement, stronger and more binding than an announcement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宣告、宣言」，语气庄重、更具约束力，强于 announcement。

entries.definition: A short official news report issued regularly or urgently.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简报、公告」，指定期或紧急发布的简短官方消息。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ment ending and the five places an announcement is actually read.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 -ment 词尾，以及公告实际被读到的五个场所。

normal.en: Announce plus -ment: the act becomes a thing you can pin to a board.
normal.cn: announce 加 -ment：动作变成了可以钉在告示板上的东西。

normal.en: An announcement is read in a hall, a newspaper, a radio, a station and a family column.
normal.cn: 公告会在礼堂、报纸、电台、车站与家庭启事栏里被读到。

normal.en: Make an announcement is the fixed verb frame; you do not say do an announcement.
normal.cn: make an announcement 是固定动词搭配，不说 do an announcement。

normal.en: Birth announcement turns private family news into a public form.
normal.cn: birth announcement 把私人的家庭消息变成公开形式。

normal.en: An announcer is the person; an announcement is the text or the spoken message.

abstract.en: Picture a small box in a newspaper where a family writes one line of news for strangers.

examples.cn: 一则响亮的广播通知告知乘客，末班车将从二号站台开出。

definition_zh: 使恼怒；使烦恼；打扰；纠缠；使不适
definition_en: to make someone feel slightly angry or irritated, especially by repeated or unwanted actions
core_image: 一只小虫在耳边绕来绕去，赶走又回来
scene: 图书馆里，邻座的人不停翻动塑料包装，声音在安静中格外刺耳。The repeated rustling began to annoy everyone at the long table.
sceneCN: 这里 annoy 是「使恼怒、使心烦」（第 1 个义项：反复的小干扰让人恼火）；句意为反复的窸窣声开始让长桌旁所有人都心烦。画面里有安静的图书馆、塑料包装与皱眉的读者。

pos.zh: 动词：使恼怒；使烦恼；打扰；纠缠
动词（旧义）：令人烦恼；使人不快

由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「感到恼火的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的」
